messages.content: You design amateur rockets that fly on certified commercial motors. Work through the design, check it with the tools, and give the final design as JSON inside <design> tags. Only report results the tools returned.
So here's the deal: Must reach at least 200 m. The biggest motor I can use is an F. I only have 24 mm hardware. Winds are typically 6 m/s. Thanks!

messages.reasoning_content:
1. Understand: Apogee at least 200 m. Motor class F at most. Only 24 mm hardware, so the motor diameter stays at or under 0.024 m. Wind is 6 m/s, so that goes in every simulation. Rail and site are not stated: 1.5 m vertical rail, sea level. Landing is not stated, so the 6 m/s gate applies.

2. Feasibility: 200 m is a small target for an E or even a D. Drag-free speed is sqrt(2 * 9.81 * 200) = 62.6 m/s. An F is allowed but not required. A 24 mm E in a modest tube clears 200 m with room and stays inside both limits. Wind 6 m/s is under the 8.94 m/s gate. Looking up a 24 mm E and a 24 mm F.

2. Feasibility: E12 is an Estes E, 27.1 N*s and 11.2 N, 24 mm, delays 4, 6 and 8 s. F24W is an AeroTech F, 47.3 N*s and 24.0 N, also 24 mm, delays 4 and 7 s. Both fit the hardware and the class ceiling. The E's 11.2 N is thin on a 1.5 m rail once the rocket is much over 0.12 kg, so I will use the F24W. Class F is the ceiling, not over it.

3. Size: 29 mm cardboard so a 26 mm mount fits around the 24 mm motor. Liftoff guess 0.15 kg. Thrust-to-weight is 24.0 / (0.15 * 9.81) = 16.3. Weight is 0.15 * 9.81 = 1.47 N, rail acceleration (24.0 - 1.47) / 0.15 = 150 m/s^2, exit speed sqrt(2 * 150 * 1.5) = 21.2 m/s. Chute for about 0.12 kg at 5 m/s: area 2 * 0.12 * 9.81 / (1.225 * 0.8 * 25) = 0.096 m^2, diameter sqrt(4 * 0.096 / pi) = 0.35 m. I will fly 0.40 m. Delay 7 s. Wind 6 m/s.

4. Draft: 29 mm tube 0.32 m, ogive nose, three balsa fins, AeroTech F24W with a 7 s delay, 0.40 m chute. Wind 6 m/s, 1.5 m rail.

4. Check: Altitude is not the problem. The simulator gives 800.1 m, well above 200 m. Margin is -0.03 cal at rail exit and through the burn. The rocket is unstable. Landing is 3.6 m/s. Rail exit is 32.4 m/s, thrust-to-weight 24.0. Impulse is 47.3 N*s, class F, and the motor is 24 mm. Wind is 6 m/s. The chute opened at 9.1 s, just before apogee at 9.38 s, at 4.6 m/s. Drift is 1287 m, with no drift cap.

5. Fix: The failing value is margin -0.03 cal. The fins are too small for a short tube with the motor at the tail. One change: span to 0.09 m and root to 0.12 m. That will add drag and the apogee will fall, but 200 m is a long way below 800 m. Motor, tube and chute stay.

4. Check: Bigger fins barely moved the margin. The simulator gives 0.01 cal, still under 1.0. Apogee fell to 642.8 m, still well above 200 m. Landing is 3.8 m/s. Rail exit is 32.3 m/s, thrust-to-weight 22.5. The fin area is adding tail mass about as fast as it adds CP.

5. Fix: The failing value is margin 0.01 cal. One change: 0.02 kg of clay at the top of the tube. Fins stay where they are. The altitude has hundreds of metres of room above 200 m, and a little nose mass will not spend it. Motor and wind stay.

4. Check: Clay cleared the margin and the altitude stayed far above the floor. The simulator gives 656.7 m, above 200 m. Margin is 1.06 cal at rail exit and through the burn. Landing is 4.2 m/s, under 6 m/s. Rail exit is 29.6 m/s, thrust-to-weight 19.0. Impulse is 47.3 N*s, class F, motor diameter 0.024 m. The chute opened at 9.1 s, just after apogee at 8.98 s, at 2.9 m/s. The section reached the ground. Wind is 6 m/s.

5. Fix: nothing left that fails.

6. Uncertainty: Liftoff mass is 0.129 kg. The first two fin sizes left the margin near zero, and 0.02 kg of clay is what crossed 1.0 cal. It is only 1.06 cal, close to the floor. Chute Cd is 0.8. Drift is 853 m in 6 m/s wind, and the prompt did not cap it.

The motor is a 24 mm class F. Wind in the flight is 6 m/s.
